newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on liquidity drain.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on liquidity drain.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates reversed earlier falls to close up 35 basis points at 23.85 percent on Tuesday after the central bank drained liquidity from the system, traders said.

"Banco de Mexico's decision to purchase paper (to drain liquidity) hauled up rates. Furthermore, as it is a Tuesday, some players try to jack up rates before placing bids for the primary auction," a trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 20 basis points at 25.00 percent.

The central bank drained 4.397 billion pesos from the market during the session by purchasing paper through five auctions, which it assigned at average rates ranging from 25.01 percent to 25.75 percent.

A Reuters survey of money market dealers showed they forecast an average assignment rate of 23.75 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates) at the primary auction later in the day, which would be a fall of 49 basis points since last week.
Traders said that secondary rates could continue to fall in coming sessions despite Tuesday's gain due to foreign capital flowing into Mexico.
"The peso is very firm despite rates falling, which shows that a substantial amount of funds is flowing in," a trader said.
Nonetheless, traders said the current excess of paper in the system could force rates back up if the peso were to weaken.
"Rates will continue to decline as long as the peso is stable, but we will need to look carefully at demand for paper at this evening's auction," a trader said.
Liquidity of 699 million pesos was expected to return to the system on Wednesday.
